title: Weekly Leads: Sprint Health & Ops Notes — 2026-05-28
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional engineering leads weekly sync
Date: 2026-05-28 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #lead-weekly-channel
Facilitator: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Natarajan, Alex Kim, Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz (observability), Tom Reed (SRE, joined for incident review)
Notes and highlights
1) Quick status pulse (round-robin)
- Platform-engineering: Core rollout of autoscale policy UI for Dedicated is in feature-complete; UX polish pending. Blocking: cloud quota verification for us-west reserved nodes (infra ticket opened).
- Serving-runtime: Latency regressions seen on 8k-sequence QA workload in staging; root cause narrows to KV cache GC interaction with new attention kernel. Investigation ongoing (ENG-4521).
- Observability: New per-route token-cost dashboards pushed to staging, sampling change increases ingestion by ~12% — cost impact estimated and shared.
- Private deployments: One enterprise pilot (FinSys) requested HSM integration timeline — legal needs uplift for contract; anticipated 6-week delivery if scope limited.
- SRE: Postmortem for 2026-05-25 capacity spike ready for review; recommended changes to burst policy defaults.
2) Incident review (Tom)
- Summary: 2026-05-25 transient tail-latency spike on hosted-api during a large synthetic run. Root cause: coordinated warm-up requests bypassing prefix cache + scheduler exhaustion on a handful of hosts.
- Mitigations applied: throttling synthetic runs via rate-limiter rule; temporary increase in warm-up pool.
- Action: Add synthetic-run detection flagging to routing layer (owner: Samir; due: 2026-06-04).
3) Cross-team dependencies & active blockers
- Quota validation for Dedicated (platform infra) blocking Reserved node provisioning in us-west (owner: Alex). Impact: delayed customer onboarding for 2 commitments. Escalation: cloud-account owner engaged; target ETA 2026-06-02.
- Attention kernel merge causes KV cache TTL edge-case in long-context models (owner: Diego + serving-runtime eng). Temporary rollback considered for the kernel change if fix not in by 2026-06-01.
- Observability ingestion increase: need confirmation of retention tiers from product before enabling in prod (owner: Priya).
4) Decisions made
- Approved controlled rollout of autoscale UI to 10% of Dedicated customers next week with telemetry gating. (Owner: Maya to coordinate with product ops)
- Do not rollback attention-kernel across prod yet; prefer targeted fixes in staging and a canary on non-critical model traffic. (Owner: Diego)
5) Action items (owners & due dates)
- Samir: Add synthetic-run detection to routing layer + alert rule (due 2026-06-04)
- Alex: Drive cloud quota verification for us-west reserved nodes; update by 2026-06-02
- Diego: Prepare targeted test harness for KV cache GC with attention kernel; deliver results 2026-06-01
- Priya: Finalize observability retention tiers and cost-analysis doc; share by 2026-06-03 (linked CONFLUENCE-DRIVERS-78)
- Maya: Draft customer-facing note describing autoscale UI rollout and expectations (due 2026-06-01)
- Lena: Add token-costs per-route view to team home dashboards and add a sample alert for >20% deviation week-over-week (due 2026-06-05)
6) Risk register (short)
- Customer onboarding delay risk (medium) — due to quota / provisioning issues for Dedicated; workaround: manual pre-provisioning on request.
- Regressions from new kernels (high until fixed) — risk of SLA violation for long-context customers. Contingency: canary, staged rollout, option to pin older kernel for sensitive customers.
- Observability cost creep (low-medium) — need budget sign-off before enabling broader retention.
7) Metrics snapshot (quick)
- 95th p50 token latency (hosted-api): 120ms -> spiked to 210ms during incident window
- Average tokens-per-second across serving fleet: 1.9M TPS (week avg)
- Autoscale queued requests: median queue time 30ms, p99 1.2s
- Observability ingestion: staging change +12% events/day (cost estimate sent to finance)
8) Roadmap/near-term milestones to watch
- 2026-06-08: Dedicated autoscale UI wider rollout (after telemetry gating)
- 2026-06-15: KV cache GC fix candidate + non-critical canary
- 2026-06-22: Private deployment HSM scoping call with FinSys legal/procurement
9) Open questions / discussion items for next week
- Do we need a temporary capacity buffer for long-context model customers to avoid SLA risk during kernel rollout? (input: SRE)
- Should we gate observability retention increases behind a beta program with opt-in customers? (input: product & finance)
- Are there ways to reduce ingestion cost with sampling logic applied at ingress vs downstream? (input: observability)
10) Parking lot (not discussed in detail)
- Proposal: standardized template for customer-facing rollout notes (product ops + comms)
- Proposal: runbook for warm-up-synthetic detection and throttling policy
Appendices / quick links
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.company/postmortem/2026-05-25-capacity-spike
- Kernel investigation tracker: JIRA-ENG-4521
- Autoscale UI PR: https://git.company/repo/infra/pull/412
Next meeting: 2026-06-04 10:00 PT
Prepared by: Maya Chen (platform-engineering lead)
Notes: rough draft — will fold in SRE postmortem comments and Diego's kernel test results before publishing final.
